group.passage:
Most of us learned to write with a pencil, and many of us still keep one close at hand. Yet there is no lead at all inside a “lead” pencil. Its dark center is actually a blend of graphite, a form of carbon, and clay. Unlike real lead, which can poison people, graphite is perfectly [[1]]. So why do people today still use the old [[2]] “lead”? The answer goes back more than four hundred years.
In the sixteenth century, people in northern England found a shiny black material in the ground. Because it looked and felt much like lead, they [[3]] it for that metal. People soon began cutting the material into sticks for writing and drawing. However, the sticks were so [[4]] that they broke easily, and they left black marks all over the user’s hands. To solve this problem, people [[5]] the sticks in string. Later, they placed them inside wooden holders, which led to the pencil we know today.
The next big step came from France near the end of the eighteenth century. An inventor there found that graphite powder could be [[6]] with clay and water to form a paste, which was then shaped and baked. By changing the [[7]] of clay in the paste, makers could control how hard the pencil was. More clay produced a harder pencil and lighter lines, while less clay produced darker lines.
In the nineteenth century, an American inventor [[8]] the idea of attaching a small rubber eraser to the end of a pencil. Because pencil marks can be erased easily, pencils are an [[9]] choice for sketching or solving math problems. Even in a world full of computers, the pencil remains a handy [[10]] for students and artists alike.

translation_zh.text:
我們大多數人都是用鉛筆學寫字的，很多人現在也還隨手放著一支。然而，「鉛」筆裡其實一點鉛也沒有。它黑色的筆芯其實是石墨（一種碳）和黏土的混合物。真正的鉛會讓人中毒，石墨卻完全安全。那麼，為什麼人們到今天還沿用「鉛」這個舊名稱呢？答案要追溯到四百多年前。
十六世紀時，英格蘭北部的人在地底發現一種閃亮的黑色物質。因為它的外觀和觸感都很像鉛，人們就把它誤認為那種金屬。不久，人們開始把這種物質切成條狀，用來書寫和畫畫。然而，這些筆芯太軟，很容易折斷，還會把使用者的手弄得滿是黑印。為了解決這個問題，人們用細繩把筆芯包起來。後來，他們把筆芯放進木製的筆桿裡，才有了今天我們熟悉的鉛筆。
下一個重大進展在十八世紀末出現在法國。那裡的一位發明家發現，石墨粉可以和黏土、水混合成糊狀，再塑形、烘烤。藉由改變糊料中黏土的量，製造者就能控制筆芯的硬度。黏土越多，筆芯越硬、線條越淡；黏土越少，線條就越深。
十九世紀時，一位美國發明家想出了在鉛筆末端裝上小橡皮擦的點子。由於鉛筆的筆跡很容易擦掉，鉛筆是素描或解數學題的理想選擇。即使在充滿電腦的世界裡，鉛筆對學生和藝術家來說，依然是一項順手的工具。
